title: UEREMCP Batch Plan
description: The `specification` payload for action=execute_plan. Batching is first-class (master prompt §2.3): one request, many dependent operations, one consolidated result. Owned by WS-05. Prior art to audit before changing this: REAgentTools `execute_editor_batch` ($ref chaining, dry_run, 8 allowlisted actions) and Epic's `ProgrammaticToolset.execute_tool_script`.

compile_policy.description: Compilation is expensive. 'at_boundaries' compiles only where a later operation depends on a compiled result — the pattern REAgentTools' NIAGARA_BATCHING.md found necessary. 'per_operation' is the slow, safe fallback.

on_failure.description: 'continue_independent' attempts operations that do not transitively depend on the failed one, and yields partially_completed.

id.description: Unique within the plan. Used by depends_on and by $ref result substitution.

depends_on.description: Operation ids that must complete first. The executor topologically sorts; a cycle is rejected before ANY operation runs.

specification.description: Action-specific, same as the top-level envelope. May contain $ref substitutions (see below).

optional.description: If true, failure does not fail the plan; it is reported and dependents are skipped.

condition.description: Run only if satisfied; otherwise the operation is skipped with a stated reason. Keeps agents from needing a round trip just to branch.

$comment: PROVISIONAL pending WS-02 audit of REAgentTools execute_editor_batch and Epic execute_tool_script (docs/proposals/ws-05-batch-grammar-blocked.md). $ref substitution: any object of the form {"$ref": "<operation_id>.<dotted.path.into.that.operation's.response>"} is replaced with the referenced value before the operation executes. Resolution failure fails the operation rather than substituting null — a silently-null asset path produces a broken asset that validates. This mirrors the *idea* behind REAgentTools' $ref convention but not necessarily its string grammar; do not finalise until the audit lands. Shared schema fragment: domains/_shared/result_ref.schema.json.
